artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
The Blue Elephant is the tenth studio album by English musician Matt Berry, released on 14 May 2021 through Acid Jazz Records. The album marks a distinct shift in Berry’s musical direction, moving away from the folk-oriented sound of his previous work toward a vibrant exploration of 1960s-inspired psychedelia, acid rock, and proto-prog. Characterized by lush Mellotron textures, swirling organ lines, and dreamy, slightly disorienting arrangements, the album evokes the spirit of late-60s British pop and psychedelic rock. Berry’s songwriting here is both nostalgic and inventive, blending vintage influences with his own idiosyncratic style.

Within Berry’s discography, The Blue Elephant stands as a culmination of his eclectic musical interests, synthesizing elements from his earlier albums into a cohesive and ambitious psychedelic statement. Critics praised the album for its authenticity and adventurous spirit, with many highlighting its immersive production and Berry’s ability to channel the era’s sonic palette without mere pastiche. The album received strong reviews upon release, with outlets noting its triumphal take on psychedelia and its place among Berry’s most accomplished works. Commercially, it continued his streak of well-received releases, further cementing his reputation as a unique voice in contemporary rock and psychedelic music.
